newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares edge higher at close, range-bound.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares edge higher at close, range-bound.

text.p: Istanbul shares saw modest gains in range-bound trade on Friday following a three-day correction of a recent rally, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed up four points, or 0.2 percent firmer at 2,010 after moving between 1,998 and 2,029. Over the week, it dropped 0.8 percent after last week's 5.68 percent gain.
Daily volume rose to 25.83 trillion lira ($167 million), compared to Wednesday's 20.78 trillion lira.

"Demand for blue chip shares of state and energy firms remained weak, so the index was squeezed in a tight band. However the 2,000 level of the index has proven to be a firm support after today's test," Murat Turgut from BAB Securities said.
"Mid-year profit forecasts of companies as well as government moves awaited next week also kept the market positive," he added.

The index slipped 1.8 percent in the past three days after soaring 30.5 percent and hitting 10 records to Monday's all-time high close of 2,043 from June 18 when the former Islamist-led coalition government resigned.
The correction began on Tuesday after the new coalition won a confidence vote in parliament last Saturday.

"Radical economic measures awaited from the new government will dominate the market. Particularly, efforts to speed up lagging privatisation and efforts to minimise the expected huge budget deficit will be the major issues in the coming weeks," said Ibrahim Basnur from Ar Securities.
"If the government succeeds in creating positive expectations before proposing early elections, then the index could reach a high of 2,500 in the near future," he concluded.

Of the 246 shares traded, gainers outdid losers by 122 to 49 and 75 finished unchanged. The IMKB Industrial gained 1.14 percent to 1,955, the IMKB Services edged up 0.1 percent to 1,928 and the IMKB Financial eased 0.19 percent to 2,151.
The index representing the transportation sector was the leading gainer with a 6.63 percent premium.
Actives were led by largely state-owned oil refiner Tupras, up 1,500 lira at 18,000 and Turkish Airlines, up 2,500 lira at 42,000. They made up 15.1 percent of the total volume.
